solver_contract.claim_boundary: Execution/interface and channel-independence control only; not a SAT/H(s)H physical validation and not a dynamic transport/holonomy result.

units_dimensions.R: same benchmark length unit as centers
units_dimensions.r_c: same benchmark length unit as centers
units_dimensions.rho: same benchmark length unit as centers

quantity_definitions.r_c: circumradius of the center triangle; distance from reconstructed circumcenter to any input center
quantity_definitions.rho: residual radius of the common intersection in the orthogonal complement when G >= 0; rho = R*sqrt(G) = sqrt(R^2-r_c^2)
quantity_definitions.terminology_guard: Do not use unqualified 'carrier radius' for r_c or rho in this case contract. Name the quantity explicitly.

assumptions: equilateral center fixture in the x-y plane embedded in R4
F2 x-w rotation is supplied as an independent frame channel and is not an input to the Three-Spheres carrier reconstruction
expected_invariants: Three-Spheres carrier result is invariant under the F2-only x-w frame perturbation
G = 2/3 for the equilateral R=1 control
static relative-frame loop telescopes to identity within floating tolerance
failure_conditions: Three-Spheres carrier output changes under frame-only perturbation
analytic G, r_c, or rho control fails outside declared tolerance
numerical certification is not CERTIFIED for the regular equilateral fixture
visual diagnostic implies that its x-y projection displays the hidden x-w frame rotation
r_c and rho are conflated under an untyped carrier-radius label

visual_contract.projection: x-y control-plane projection of the three equal-radius sphere cross-sections and reconstructed center circumcenter
hidden_channels: residual common-intersection circle/sphere radius rho unless separately rendered
visual_contract.question_for_nathan: Does this projected equilateral Three-Spheres control depict the intended center/carrier fixture? The x-w frame perturbation should be invisible in this solver view; rho is a distinct residual-intersection quantity and is not represented by the center-to-circumcenter distance r_c.
